property_summary: After a successful Put of positive msg.value, the contract's recorded balance for the sender equals the amount put (i.e., Acc[thisAddr].balance == depositedAmount).

For any caller and any provided _unlockTime and msg.value, the reference contract guarantees that after Put(...) the caller's stored unlockTime is at least block.timestamp (i.e., acc.unlockTime >= block.timestamp); the mutant allows setting acc.unlockTime to a past time (< block.timestamp) for some inputs, breaking this invariant.

After any call to Put(...) by any sender with any value, the reference contract ensures the sender's stored unlockTime is >= block.timestamp; the mutant allows acc.unlockTime < block.timestamp for some inputs (it accepts the provided _unlockTime even if in the past).

For any caller, after calling Put(...) the reference contract guarantees the caller's stored unlockTime is >= block.timestamp (it clamps to now), while the mutant can set unlockTime to a past value (< block.timestamp) when given such _unlockTime, violating the invariant.

For any caller and any input, after calling Put(_unlockTime) the reference contract ensures Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime >= block.timestamp (it clamps to now), whereas the mutant can set Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime < block.timestamp when given a past _unlockTime, violating this invariant.

For any caller and inputs, after calling Put(_unlockTime) the reference contract ensures Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime >= block.timestamp (it clamps to now); the mutant that assigns acc.unlockTime = _unlockTime can make Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime < block.timestamp for some inputs, violating this invariant.

After calling Put(x) the contract's Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime is never set to a time earlier than block.timestamp at the time of the call (i.e., correct C sets unlockTime to max(_unlockTime, now) so unlockTime >= now), whereas the mutant unconditionally sets it to now which can make future behavior different when _unlockTime > now (the rule: unlockTime >= now always holds; mutant may set it to exactly now, breaking intended preservation of a larger _unlockTime).

For any caller, when calling Put(_unlockTime, value) the contract preserves a non-decreasing unlockTime: the resulting Acc[msg].unlockTime is at least the previous Acc[msg].unlockTime and at least the block.timestamp at the time of the call; the mutant that unconditionally sets unlockTime = block.timestamp can decrease a previously larger unlockTime to now and thus violates the non-decreasing property for some inputs.

For any caller and any _unlockTime and deposit value, calling Put(_) never decreases the caller's stored unlockTime below its prior value nor below the current block.timestamp (i.e., new unlockTime >= old unlockTime and >= now); the mutant that unconditionally sets unlockTime = now can decrease a previously larger unlockTime, violating this non-decreasing property for some inputs.

After calling Put(...) from an address, the reference contract sets Acc[addr].unlockTime to be either the supplied _unlockTime if it's in the future or to now, so the resulting unlockTime equals max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp) — the mutant that always sets unlockTime = block.timestamp will make the stored unlockTime strictly less than the supplied _unlockTime whenever _unlockTime > block.timestamp; the test asserts that when _unlockTime > block.timestamp the stored unlockTime equals _unlockTime (reference) and the mutant will violate it for some fuzzed inputs.

For any caller and input, calling Put with a future _unlockTime preserves that future time in the public Acc mapping (i.e., after Put returns, Acc[msg].unlockTime equals the supplied _unlockTime whenever _unlockTime > block.timestamp at call time); the mutant that always sets unlockTime = block.timestamp will make Acc[msg].unlockTime != _unlockTime for some fuzzed future _unlockTime.

For any caller and any msg.value, after calling Put(u) the caller's Acc[msg.sender].balance increases by exactly msg.value (i.e., new balance = old balance + msg.value); the mutant that omits incrementing balance breaks this rule for inputs with msg.value>0.

For any caller and any positive ETH sent to Put, the contract's public Acc[msg.sender].balance increases by at least the sent amount (i.e., new balance >= old balance + msg.value); the mutant that omits the balance increment violates this for some inputs with msg.value>0.

After a successful Put call that sends zero wei, the holder's stored unlockTime is set to at least the current block.timestamp (i.e., acc.unlockTime >= block.timestamp); the mutant still updates unlockTime but leaves balance unchanged so this rule still holds for zero-value calls — to distinguish, we instead assert that when nonzero ETH is sent, the contract's total recorded balance for the sender equals the contract's observed balance for that sender (address(c).balance contribution), which the mutant breaks because it fails to record the sent ETH in Acc mapping while the contract balance increases.

For any caller and any sent ETH, after Put the contract's on-chain ETH balance increases by the sent amount and the public per-address recorded Acc[msg.sender].balance equals the sum of all prior recorded deposits for that address; the mutant that omits incrementing acc.balance causes a mismatch between address(c).balance (which does increase) and the public Acc balance for that sender for some inputs.

For any caller and any nonzero msg.value sent to Put, the contract's total ETH balance (address(c).balance) increases by msg.value and the contract's public mapping Acc for that caller records that same amount (i.e., Acc[caller].balance increases by msg.value), whereas the mutant that omits incrementing acc.balance will make address(c).balance increase while Acc[caller].balance does not, so comparing address(c).balance delta vs Acc[caller].balance delta distinguishes them.

For any caller and any sent value, calling Put sets Acc[caller].balance equal to the previous balance plus msg.value (i.e., it increases by exactly the deposited amount); the mutant doubles the resulting stored balance and thus violates this rule for some inputs.

For any caller and deposit amount, calling Put increases Acc[caller].balance by exactly msg.value (new balance = old balance + msg.value); the mutant that doubles acc.balance after adding msg.value violates this rule for some inputs.

For any depositor and deposit amount, after calling Put the stored Acc[depositor].balance is at least the prior balance plus msg.value (i.e., balance_new >= balance_old + msg.value); the mutant that multiplies acc.balance by 2 can make the stored balance strictly greater than that relation in ways that break the intended equality-to-or-minimum rule for some inputs.

For any depositor and deposit amount, after calling Put the stored Acc[depositor].balance equals the previous balance plus msg.value (i.e., no extra multiplication by 2); the mutant that doubles acc.balance after adding msg.value violates this equality for some inputs.

For any depositor and deposit amount, after calling Put the stored Acc[depositor].balance is divisible by msg.value (i.e., the deposited increment divides the resulting balance); the mutant that doubles acc.balance can produce resulting balances that are still divisible in many cases but will violate divisibility for some fuzzed msg.value inputs (e.g., when msg.value is an odd number and previous balance is zero), causing the property to fail.

After a successful Collect call by a depositor, the depositor's recorded Acc balance equals the contract's prior recorded balance minus the collected amount (i.e., Collect atomically reduces stored balance before sending funds).

If this test contract deposited at least MinSum and attempts to collect no more than it deposited, then Collect should not revert (i.e., not reverted).
If this test contract deposited at least MinSum and attempts to collect no more than it deposited, then Collect should not revert (i.e., reverted == false).
If this test contract deposited at least MinSum and attempts to collect no more than it deposited, then Collect should not revert (i.e., reverted == false).

After a successful Collect call the stored balance for the caller always equals the prior balance minus the withdrawn amount (i.e. acc.balance decreases by _am); the mutant that sends funds before updating acc.balance can be reentered and cause the final stored balance to differ.
